reachable: Partly, and the reachable part is not the claimed part. Gradient reaches everything: `out_scale` is trained by the main loss because `contrib` is added into `pred` at command positions (verified by a nonzero prediction delta once out_scale is un-zeroed), and the head's retrieval plus the arch's shared transition operator are trained by the aux — `aux_loss` returns 1.5998 at full ramp on a real 16-sequence batch from data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd, mining 46 examples out of 474 active steps. The arch DOES expose `transition_from_emb` (r22_retrieval_composition_renderer inherits it from R18PathStateLatentTransition), so the trans term is live rather than silently disabled. But the path to the SCORED read is degenerate: the head's output there is a single board-determined vector scaled by a read-command-dependent scalar, and it cannot express "the content at location Y" versus "the content at location Z" at all. Worse for interpretation of any score: that vector still changes between the native and role-swapped arms, because re-encoding the mv commands changes the slot keys and the running mean. The head is therefore exactly the class of predictor the ground truth warns about — one keyed on chain position rather than on the read location — which does not cancel structurally on the frozen slice. A positive comp_ca from this candidate would not be evidence for the hypothesised copy-transport mechanism.
solves_outside_model: No. I traced every input to both entry points. `_CopyTransportMemory.run` takes only `tok` (frozen standardized embeddings) and `key_pad`; it never receives a command string and there is no string handling in the module. `aux_loss` reads only `batch["tok"]`, `batch["key_pad"]`, and the tensor keys `_layout_ok` checks (types/tgt/cmd_mask) — no `cmds`, no path parsing, no `.split()` anywhere in the file (grepped). The mining is done entirely on observation-embedding squared distances under `torch.no_grad()`: it detects duplicate observations and steps with oversized duplicate clusters (the empty renders), and it uses that only to select WHICH steps get an extra loss term. Its positive target is `truth = obs[b_i, t_i]` — that step's own observation, which the main loss already supervises at that command position — so it adds no routing answer the harness was not already providing. Nothing resolves an mv chain in Python, and nothing extra enters the forward pass at scoring time. This is loss shaping and sample selection, the legitimate side of the line, and it is structurally unlike the retracted stream cheat.
summary: Most of this candidate is exactly what it says. I verified by execution: bit-for-bit init identity with the unwrapped arch (max diff 0.0); the closed-form recursion really is solved, not unrolled (residual 1.19e-7 on V = m·att·V + (1−m)·obs, att strictly lower-triangular, unit diagonal, so depth costs nothing); copy-not-edit holds (no learned transform sits between a source content and a destination slot value); query-side centering is strictly causal (inclusive cumsum up to i, no future command touches the query at i) and key-side centering would indeed cancel in the softmax; the null column and log-occupancy bias broadcast over the key axis correctly; the NCE decision variable is squared-L2/dim, matching the eval's `_nway`; the duplicate/contentless mining is calibrated exactly as described and works on the real training root (contentless clusters of 8-14 versus contentful ≤3, clean separation at max_dup=3; 44 of 46 mined earlier-duplicates are byte-identical embeddings); and the transition-consistency aux is live, not disabled. Nothing computes the routing outside the model. But the central mechanism — the one every other claim exists to serve — does not operate at the position that is scored. `active = live_cmd & live_obs`, and at the read the observation is withheld by construction, so the read's path signature is zeroed and the retrieval query collapses to the negated running mean of the earlier signatures. Replacing the read command with a completely different embedding changes the retrieved content by exactly zero. The head's whole contribution at the scored read is one board-determined vector times a scalar gate; it cannot address a location. The addressing is trained in a regime (cmd and obs both present) that the scored position never occupies. Claim (c), the piece the author calls "the crux", is unreachable as written.

divergences.claim: "My head's prediction at the read is the content standing in the slot that the chain of writes deposited there" and claim (c): the destination slot "is found later by `cat Y` because the mv command literally contains the whole string Y: a full-path match beats the prefix-only match a name-sibling lure can offer."
divergences.what_the_code_does: At the scored read position the retrieval query contains ZERO information about the read command, so no `cat Y` query exists and no full-path match can happen. `run()` computes `active = live_cmd & live_obs` and then `p = _unit(self.addr(cf)) * af.unsqueeze(-1)`. At scoring, build_cups_layout marks the read command valid and withholds its observation, so `active[read] = False`, `af = 0`, and `p[read] = 0`. The query becomes `u[read] = _unit(0 - sigmoid(center_logit) * running_mean) = -unit(prefix mean of signatures)` — a direction fixed by the board prefix alone. Everything downstream (`scores = u @ p.T`, `att`, `reads`) is therefore identical no matter which location is read. The read command's only remaining influence is the scalar `gate = sigmoid(read_gate(cf))`, so the head's entire contribution at the scored read is one board-determined vector times a scalar. This regime also never occurs in training (collate clears cmd and obs together), so the addressing is trained in one regime and evaluated in a strictly different one.
divergences.evidence: Executed against the real modules. (1) Perturbing ONLY tok[0, 2r] (the read command) across 5 different random embeddings: `reads[0, r]` byte-identical every time; relative change = 0.0 exactly. Contrast: perturbing an ACTIVE earlier command's own token changes its slot read by 0.76 relative. (2) `||p[read]|| = 0.0`; `cos(u_read under two different read commands) = 1.0`; `torch.allclose(u1[read], u2[read]) = True`. (3) With out_scale un-zeroed, contrib at the read across 5 different read commands is exactly a scalar multiple of one fixed vector (scalars 1.000/1.031/1.122/0.965/1.046; max residual off the scalar model 1.5e-8). (4) A minimal repair I verified on a /tmp copy — build the query from command liveness (`q = unit(addr(cf)) * live_cmd`, centering still over the obs-gated `p`) and use `n = (L+1)//2` — restores read-command dependence: relative change 0.36 instead of 0.0.

divergences.claim: Implicit in "Every command position opens exactly one slot" and in the read mechanism: the read command position participates in the slot memory.
divergences.what_the_code_does: `n = L // 2`, and the cups layout has odd length `Lmax = 2*rmax + 1`, so the command slice `tok[:, 0::2]` (rmax+1 columns) is truncated to rmax. For a window with r == rmax the read command is dropped from the memory entirely, and the contrib write `k = min(contrib.size(1), cmd_view.size(1))` never reaches that column: the head adds exactly nothing at the scored read for the deepest window.
divergences.evidence: Executed: with rmax=5, a row with r=5 gets |delta| = 0.000000e+00 at read position 10 while a row with r=3 gets 8.99e+00 at position 6. Impact on the real slice is negligible — parsed data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd/val.jsonl: 1280 cups windows, rmax = 28, exactly 1 window at r=28, and 0 of the 498 depth-3/4 eligible windows sit at rmax. So this is a latent bug, not a scoring problem today.

divergences.claim: Module DESCRIPTION: "adds each slot's log write-occupancy so only written slots can answer"; hypothesis (c): "Occupancy does the disambiguation at run time, from the model's own memory state."
divergences.what_the_code_does: `occ = sigmoid(self.occ_gate(pair))` where `pair = cat([gelu(cmd_feat(c)), gelu(obs_feat(o))])` — a learned per-step gate on that step's own (command, observation) features, bias-initialised to 1.5 so sigmoid ≈ 0.82 uniformly. It counts nothing, and it receives no input about whether any earlier command wrote to that path. Every active command position opens a slot with essentially equal occupancy at init, so "only written slots can answer" is vacuous. The disambiguation the hypothesis actually needs — that a move's destination has no slot — comes from causal masking (`reachable = j < i`), i.e. from the fact that no earlier command mentions the fresh destination name, not from the occ term.
divergences.evidence: Read of `_CopyTransportMemory.__init__` / `run`; `self.occ_gate = nn.Linear(2 * h, 1)` with `nn.init.constant_(self.occ_gate.bias, 1.5)` and no other occupancy computation anywhere in the file. The term is a legitimate learnable suppressor; the name and the DESCRIPTION overstate it as a write count.

divergences.claim: "Extra forward cost is dominated by two Linear(768, 128) maps ... roughly a quarter of the arch's own per-step cost by parameter count."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Head parameters total 206,470 against 3,735,451 for the arch — 5.5%, not ~25%. The author flagged this as an arithmetic estimate rather than a measurement, and the error is in the harmless direction.
divergences.evidence: Measured with the real build: `sum(p.numel() for p in mod.parameters()) = 206470`; arch (excluding copy_transport) `= 3735451`; ratio 0.0553.
